newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela office sees 0.8 pct GDP budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela office sees 0.8 pct GDP budget surplus.

text.p: Venezuela expects to post a 0.8 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) budget surplus in 1997, Maraima Padron, director of the Central Budget Office (Ocepre) told Reuters.
The surplus will come despite a recent 75 percent civil servant wage increase that exceeds previously budgeted salary expenses of 1.3 trillion bolivars by 15 percent, Padron said.
"Our objective remains a modest budget surplus, of at least 0.8 percent of GDP," she said in an interview.

Padron added the government was working on cutting some 300 billion bolivars from other areas in the budget to compensate for the extra spending, "and although that's not easy we are making progress".

Some 82 billion bolivar in cuts are to be considered Wednesday by the Cabinet, she said, and planned spending remains at 7.8 trillion bolivars as approved by congress late last year -- even though total revenues could be as high as nine trillion.
"That doesn't mean we'll spend the whole nine trillion, we want to respect the 7.8 trillion roof".
For example, Padron said the government would receive up to 900 billion bolivars from state oil company PdVSA later this month, of which only 49 billion had been previously expected.
"The rest is being treated as fresh revenue," she said.
The government's recent wage increase has raised fears among analysts of spiraling costs, a bust budget and soaring inflation.
While the Central Bank has said the country's official inflation target for the year remains 25 percent, Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff has said inflation will be between 30 and 35 percent.
